newsitem.title: USA: U.S. shuttle launches on mission to Mir.
newsitem.headline: U.S. shuttle launches on mission to Mir.

text.p: The space shuttle Atlantis lifted off before dawn on Sunday, headed for its fifth rendezvous with Russia's Mir space station.
The $2 billion spaceship, with six astronauts aboard, roared off its Florida launch pad in a brilliant blaze of light at 4:27 a.m. EST (0927 GMT).
Atlantis is due to dock with Mir on Tuesday night to pick up astronaut John Blaha, who has worked aboard the station since September, and drop off his replacement astronaut Jerry Linenger.

Linenger, a 41-year-old Navy captain and medical doctor, is scheduled to spend four months on Mir, where he will perform more than 80 scientific experiments. Atlantis is due to return to the station in May to bring him home.
He will be the fourth U.S. astronaut to live aboard Mir as part of a NASA effort to learn more about the effects of long duration space flight on the human body.
Atlantis' launch was the first of eight planned in 1997. The year is due to end with the first shuttle mission to assemble the NASA-led international space station.
